title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Four designs for the makerspace assistant are described below. Which one is an agent rather than a workflow?

options.text: Code always calls check_calendar, then search_manuals, then asks the model for one reply
Code asks the model to label each question, then runs the one handler for that label
The model picks each next tool from the results so far and decides when to stop
Code makes three model calls in a fixed order, each using the output of the last

items.stem: In one sentence: in terms of who decides the next step, what is the difference between a workflow and an agent?

Every booking request to your assistant goes the same way: read the machine, date and time from the student's message, check the calendar, book the slot if it is free, and send a confirmation. Which design fits best, and why?

options.text: An agent, because any task that uses tools needs a loop to run them
A fixed workflow, because the steps and their order are known in advance
An agent, because only a model in a loop can read a student's message
A fixed workflow, because workflows run without calling a language model

items.stem: Take one booking request. As a fixed workflow, the code runs check_calendar and book_machine itself and makes exactly 2 model calls (one to read the request, one to write the confirmation). As an agent, the model requests five tools one at a time, and then writes the final answer; each model call ends with one tool request or the final answer. How many more model calls does the agent make than the workflow on this request?
Which request to the makerspace assistant is the best candidate for an agent, because you cannot list its steps in advance?

options.text: "Book the 3D printer for me on Friday at 2 pm."
"What is the maximum material thickness for the laser cutter?"
"Please cancel my booking for the band saw tomorrow."
"I want to make a 20 cm acrylic sign by next week; what do I need?"

items.stem: Your sponsor gave the team a small model budget. In one sentence, give one reason a fixed workflow is the better choice for a task whose steps you can list in advance.
